name: Iran
summary: December 2025–January 2026 protests — the largest since the 1979 revolution, spreading to 200+ cities — were met with live ammunition. 3,428+ protesters were killed during peak unrest (January 8–12, 2026). Executions hit their highest level since 2015. Kurds, Baloch, and women's rights activists are disproportionately targeted in a widening crackdown.
context:
Iran's human rights crisis has intensified dramatically following a wave of protests that began in December 2025 and spread to over 200 cities — the largest domestic uprising since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The immediate trigger was economic grievances: currency collapse, chronic unemployment, and inflation. But protests quickly broadened into demands for political change and accountability for the regime's systematic repression.

The government's response was brutal. At peak unrest between January 8–12, 2026, at least 3,428 protesters were killed according to the Iran Human Rights News Agency (IHRNGO). Thousands more were injured. Mass arrests swept up students, journalists, workers, and activists. Many of those arrested have been subjected to torture in detention, according to survivor testimony and UN reports.

Iran's execution rate has been climbing for years and hit its highest point since 2015. Many executions follow trials that international observers describe as not meeting minimum standards of due process — confessions extracted under torture, charges of 'enmity against God' applied to political prisoners, and executions carried out with minimal notice.

Ethnic minorities face disproportionate repression. The Baloch — a minority in Sistan-Baluchestan province — face the highest execution rates of any group. Kurdish activists, journalists, and politicians are systematically prosecuted. Women's rights activists who participated in the 2022 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising continue to face prosecution, imprisonment, and in some cases execution.

No independent media operates inside Iran. International journalists cannot enter freely. The UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, established after the 2022 uprising, has documented crimes against humanity but faces Iranian non-cooperation.

donate.description: Documenting and reporting on human rights violations in Iran, including crackdowns on protesters, executions, and persecution of minorities.

donate.name: UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran
donate.description: Supporting the UN's independent investigation into human rights violations in Iran, including the crackdown on recent protests.

donate.description: Documenting human rights violations in Kurdish regions of Iran, including executions, disappearances, and persecution of activists.

awareness: Share that 3,428+ people were killed in the January 2026 protests — the largest civilian death toll in Iran since 1979 — in what the UN has documented as crimes against humanity
Highlight the disproportionate targeting of Kurds and Baloch: Iran's ethnic minorities face execution rates far above the national average
Amplify Iranian civil society voices in exile — journalists, activists, and academics who continue to document and advocate despite great personal risk
Raise awareness about the systematic torture of detained protesters — confessions extracted under torture are then used to execute people
Challenge the international community's insufficient response: crimes against humanity documented by the UN demand more than expressions of concern
political: Urge your government to support the renewal and strengthening of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran at the Human Rights Council
Demand targeted sanctions against specific Iranian officials responsible for ordering and carrying out the massacre of protesters
Push for universal jurisdiction prosecutions in your country for Iranian officials who travel abroad and are documented in human rights violations
Advocate for diplomatic measures that protect Iranian civil society members who remain in the country, including fast-track visas for human rights defenders
Support calls for the UN Security Council to refer Iran to the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity
